# QuadraticCharSum — on one wheel, the residue character of a pair pattern adds up to −1

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [One wheel at a time: squares, characters and the number 24](../../GRAPH.md#one-wheel-at-a-time-squares-characters-and-the-number-24)

On a prime wheel, give each position +1 if it is a nonzero square, −1 if it is not a square, and 0 at 0 (the quadratic character). For two offsets, multiply a position's distances from them and add the character of the product around the wheel: the total is −1 when the offsets sit on different positions of the wheel, and the wheel size minus 1 when they coincide. The same −1 holds for any quadratic whose discriminant is not 0, split or not. This is the exact degree-two case of the square-root bounds of Hasse and Weil (nodes HasseCurve, StepanovWeil); the proof goes through Mathlib's Jacobi sums. A classical fact, not new here.

## Claims

<a id="pair_char_sum_distinct"></a>
### `pair_char_sum_distinct`

On an odd prime wheel, the character of the product of the distances to two different offsets adds up to −1.

```lean
/-- **Two different offsets.** On an odd prime wheel, the quadratic character
of the product of the distances to two different offsets adds up to −1. -/
def pair_char_sum_distinct : Prop :=
  ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], p ≠ 2 → ∀ a b : ZMod p, a ≠ b →
    ∑ x : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((x + a) * (x + b)) = -1
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.QuadraticCharSum.pair_char_sum_distinct_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/QuadraticCharSum.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/QuadraticCharSum.lean)

<a id="pair_char_sum_equal"></a>
### `pair_char_sum_equal`

On any prime wheel, the character of the squared distance to one offset adds up to the wheel size minus 1.

```lean
/-- **Two equal offsets.** On any prime wheel, the quadratic character of the
square of the distance to one offset adds up to the wheel size minus 1. -/
def pair_char_sum_equal : Prop :=
  ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], ∀ a : ZMod p,
    ∑ x : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) ((x + a) * (x + a)) = (p : ℤ) - 1
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.QuadraticCharSum.pair_char_sum_equal_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/QuadraticCharSum.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/QuadraticCharSum.lean)

<a id="quadratic_char_sum"></a>
### `quadratic_char_sum`

On an odd prime wheel, the character of a quadratic with nonzero discriminant adds up to −1.

```lean
/-- **Any quadratic with nonzero discriminant.** On an odd prime wheel, the
quadratic character of a square plus a multiple plus a constant adds up to −1
whenever the discriminant is not 0, whether or not the quadratic splits. -/
def quadratic_char_sum : Prop :=
  ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], p ≠ 2 → ∀ b c : ZMod p, b ^ 2 - 4 * c ≠ 0 →
    ∑ x : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x ^ 2 + b * x + c) = -1
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.QuadraticCharSum.quadratic_char_sum_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/QuadraticCharSum.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/QuadraticCharSum.lean)
